newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends stable on lack of direction.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends stable on lack of direction.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed little changed against its American counterpart on Thursday amid a lack of clear direction for the local currency, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.524 against Wednesday's T$27.527 close. Turnover through dealers was a moderately active US$212 million.
Dealers noted a slowing of recently strong foreign fund entries for the stock market, which has surged in 1997.
"Foreign funds have slowed their inflows as the stock index has reached comparatively high levels after recent rallies," said one dealer.
As of Thursday, the stock index had risen some 23 percent in 1997 alone.
Dealers noted emerging quarter-end U.S. dollar demand mainly from importers, which almost balanced the impact of foreign fund inflows.
"Importers had shown keen interest when the local dollar nears the T$27.50 level," said another dealer.

"The lack of direction recently has reduced investors' interest in speculative trading, thus slowing turnover," the second dealer said. For Friday, a stable T$27.52-27.54 range was seen. -- James Peng (5080815)
